chapters.category: Ethiopic textual tradition • Modern English research translation
chapters.title: Chapter 72 — The Ordered Course of the Sun
chapters.sourceNote: Translated afresh into clear modern English from the earliest complete primary-language text responsibly available for this chapter. No extant Aramaic wording has been identified for the Astronomical Book, while the limited Greek fragments do not preserve this chapter in full. The complete Ethiopic (Geʽez) text in August Dillmann's 1851 critical edition, Liber Henoch Aethiopice, is the translation base for all thirty-seven verses: Uriel's account of the six eastern and six western portals, the sun's alternating thirty- and thirty-one-morning stations, the eighteen-part measures of day and night, the 364-day year, and the sun's unceasing obedience to the Lord's command. Numerical statements and the text's portal model are translated as given rather than conformed to a later astronomical system. No unattested wording was supplied, and no modern English translation was used as the translation base.

verses.text: This is the book of the courses of the lights of heaven: each one according to its group, authority and season, according to its name, place of origin and month. Uriel, the holy angel who was with me and is their guide, showed me their entire record exactly as it is for every year of the world and forever, until the new creation that endures forever is completed.
verses.study: The Astronomical Book begins as received instruction. Time, names and courses belong to a stable order that points beyond the present world toward enduring renewal.
crossReferences: Genesis 1:14 — heavenly lights mark signs, seasons, days and years
Isaiah 65:17 — God promises a new heavens and a new earth

verses.text: This is the first command governing the lights. The light called the sun rises through the eastern portals of heaven and sets through the western portals of heaven.
verses.study: The sun follows a command rather than ruling independently. Its daily path is service within creation.
crossReferences: Psalm 19:4–6 — the sun runs its appointed course
Ecclesiastes 1:5 — the sun rises, sets and returns

verses.text: I saw six portals through which the sun rises and six portals through which it sets. The moon also rises and sets through these portals, with the leaders of the stars and those they guide: six in the east and six at the setting of the sun, each exactly corresponding to the next. Many windows were to the right and left of those portals.
verses.study: The paired portals describe the year as ordered correspondence between east and west. The moon and stars participate in the same governed heaven.
crossReferences: Job 38:31–33 — heavenly constellations follow ordinances
Jeremiah 31:35 — sun, moon and stars serve by fixed order

verses.text: First the great light called the sun goes out. Its circle is like the circle of heaven, and its whole body is filled with fire that gives light and heat.
verses.study: The sun's grandeur is acknowledged without making it divine. Its light and warmth are created gifts.
crossReferences: Genesis 1:16 — God makes the greater light to govern the day
Psalm 74:16 — the sun belongs to the Lord who established it

verses.text: The wind drives the chariot on which it ascends. The sun descends from heaven and returns through the north to travel toward the east; it is guided so that it enters its appointed portal and shines upon the face of heaven.
verses.study: Even the unseen nightly return is portrayed as guided. The sun neither chooses its gate nor loses its way.
crossReferences: Psalm 104:3–4 — wind serves as God's messenger
Job 38:12 — dawn knows its appointed place

verses.text: In this way, in the first month it rises through the great portal, the fourth of the six eastern portals.
verses.study: The annual account begins at the fourth gate. Ordered observation gives the year a defined starting station.
crossReferences: Exodus 12:2 — the year receives an appointed first month
Psalm 104:19 — the heavenly lights mark seasons

verses.text: In that fourth portal, from which the sun rises in the first month, there are twelve open windows. A flame comes from them when they are opened at their appointed time.
verses.study: The twelve windows reinforce the union of time and light. Their opening occurs by appointment, not accident.
crossReferences: Daniel 2:21 — God changes times and seasons
Psalm 78:23 — heaven's doors open at divine command

verses.text: When the sun rises into heaven, it goes out through that fourth portal for thirty mornings, and it descends precisely through the fourth portal in the west of heaven.
verses.study: Rising and setting correspond across the heavens for a measured period. Precision is presented as a mark of faithful created service.
crossReferences: Psalm 89:37 — the faithful heavenly witness is established
James 1:17 — the Father of lights is free from shifting shadow

verses.text: During those days, the day grows longer from day to day and the night grows shorter from night to night until the thirtieth morning.
verses.study: Seasonal change occurs gradually within order. Variation need not mean disorder.
crossReferences: Genesis 8:22 — seasons continue while the earth remains
Psalm 74:17 — summer and winter are established by God

verses.text: On that day the day is two parts longer than the night: the day is exactly ten parts, and the night is eight parts.
verses.study: The chapter measures a complete day-night cycle in eighteen parts. Counting makes the changing balance intelligible.
crossReferences: John 11:9 — daylight is described in measured hours
Psalm 90:12 — rightly numbering time teaches wisdom

verses.text: The sun rises from that fourth portal and sets in the fourth, then returns to the fifth eastern portal for thirty mornings; it rises from there and sets through the fifth portal.
verses.study: The move to the fifth portal advances the annual sequence while maintaining east-west correspondence.
crossReferences: Ecclesiastes 3:1 — every matter has its season
Psalm 19:6 — the sun's circuit reaches across heaven

verses.text: Then the day lengthens by two parts and becomes eleven parts, while the night shortens and becomes seven parts.
verses.study: The increasing daylight is expressed by a new ratio. The repeated accounting emphasizes dependable progression.
crossReferences: Genesis 1:5 — day and night are distinguished and named
Jeremiah 33:20 — the covenant of day and night is dependable

verses.text: The sun returns to the east and enters the sixth portal. Because of its sign, it rises and sets through the sixth portal for thirty-one mornings.
verses.study: The thirty-one-morning station marks a turning point in the yearly pattern. Its sign identifies a meaningful celestial interval.
crossReferences: Genesis 1:14 — lights serve as signs and measures
Psalm 104:19 — the moon and sun know appointed times

verses.text: On that day the day is longer than the night; the day is twice the night. The day becomes twelve parts, and the night is shortened to six parts.
verses.study: At the longest-day station the eighteen parts reach their widest imbalance. Even the extreme remains measured.
crossReferences: Joshua 10:13 — extraordinary daylight remains under divine authority
Psalm 136:8 — the sun governs the day by God's appointment

verses.text: Then the sun rises so that the day begins to shorten and the night to lengthen. It returns to the east, enters the sixth portal, and rises and sets from it for thirty mornings.
verses.study: The course reverses without breaking continuity. Decrease begins from the same sixth portal where the maximum was reached.
crossReferences: Ecclesiastes 1:5–6 — created cycles continually return
Daniel 2:21 — changing seasons remain under God's rule

verses.text: When the thirty mornings are completed, the day is shortened by exactly one part and becomes eleven parts, while the night becomes seven parts.
verses.study: The measured return mirrors the earlier increase. Completion and reduction occur at their appointed count.
crossReferences: Ecclesiastes 3:1 — appointed times govern changing conditions
Psalm 104:20 — night arrives by divine ordering

verses.text: The sun goes out from that sixth portal in the west, travels east, rises through the fifth portal for thirty mornings, and again sets in the west through the fifth western portal.
verses.study: The fifth portal is revisited on the descending half of the year. Repetition makes the cycle recognizable and dependable.
crossReferences: Psalm 19:5–6 — the sun rejoices to run its repeated course
Ecclesiastes 1:5 — the sun hurries back to rise again

verses.text: On that day the day is shortened by two parts and becomes ten parts, while the night becomes eight parts.
verses.study: Day and night move closer to equality. The course gives each its due season without rivalry.
crossReferences: Genesis 1:18 — the lights govern day and night
Psalm 74:16 — both day and night belong to God

verses.text: The sun goes out through that fifth portal and sets through the fifth western portal. Then it rises through the fourth portal for thirty-one mornings because of its sign, and sets in the west.
verses.study: The fourth portal again carries a thirty-one-morning interval. The sign belongs within the recurring structure of the year.
crossReferences: Genesis 1:14 — seasons are indicated by heavenly signs
Sirach 43:6 — the heavenly light marks times and seasons

verses.text: On that day the day and night become equal. The night is nine parts, and the day is nine parts.
verses.study: Equality arrives at the midpoint of the eighteen-part measure. Balance is one appointed phase within a moving cycle.
crossReferences: Genesis 1:4–5 — light and darkness are ordered into day and night
Psalm 65:8 — dawn and evening are both made to rejoice

verses.text: The sun rises from that portal and sets in the west. It returns to the east, rises for thirty mornings through the third portal, and sets in the west through the third portal.
verses.study: The sun crosses into the year's darker half while remaining faithful to corresponding gates.
crossReferences: Job 9:7–9 — the stars and sun remain subject to their Maker
Psalm 104:19 — the sun knows its setting

verses.text: On that day the night becomes longer than the day. The night grows longer from night to night, and the day shorter from day to day, until the thirtieth morning. The night becomes exactly ten parts, and the day eight parts.
verses.study: The measured growth of darkness is not portrayed as victory over light. Both lengths follow an established order.
crossReferences: Genesis 8:22 — day and night continue in their seasons
Jeremiah 33:20 — the order of night cannot cancel the order of day

verses.text: The sun rises from that third portal and sets through the third western portal. It returns east and for thirty mornings rises through the second eastern portal; in the same way it sets through the second portal in the west of heaven.
verses.study: The second portal continues the symmetrical descent. Each movement has a corresponding destination.
crossReferences: Psalm 19:6 — the sun completes its circuit
Job 38:33 — heaven's ordinances exercise their appointed rule

verses.text: On that day the night becomes eleven parts, and the day seven parts.
verses.study: The growing night reaches a new measured station, yet the day retains its appointed portion.
crossReferences: Psalm 104:20–23 — night and day assign fitting times to creatures
John 9:4 — daylight has a bounded season for work

verses.text: On that day the sun rises from the second portal and sets through the second portal in the west. It returns east to the first portal for thirty-one mornings and sets through the first portal in the west of heaven.
verses.study: The first portal marks the furthest station in this half of the circuit. The thirty-one mornings complete the approach to the year's longest night.
crossReferences: Psalm 74:17 — the earth's boundaries and seasons are established
Acts 17:26 — appointed times and boundaries lie under divine rule

verses.text: On that day the night grows longer and becomes twice the day. The night is exactly twelve parts, and the day six parts.
verses.study: The longest night forms the inverse of the longest day. The symmetrical measure portrays a complete annual order.
crossReferences: Genesis 1:16 — the lesser and greater lights govern their domains
Psalm 136:9 — moon and stars govern the night by God's arrangement

verses.text: The sun has now completed the divisions of its course. It turns again through those divisions, enters that portal for thirty mornings, and sets in the west opposite it.
verses.study: Completion immediately becomes return. The sun's circuit is sustained through repeated obedience.
crossReferences: Ecclesiastes 1:5 — setting and return belong to one course
Psalm 148:6 — heavenly bodies keep the decree given to them

verses.text: On that day the night is shortened from its length by one part. The night becomes eleven parts, and the day seven parts.
verses.study: Light begins to increase from the year's darkest station. The reversal is precise and hopeful without leaving the established cycle.
crossReferences: Psalm 30:5 — night gives way to morning joy
Jeremiah 33:20 — day follows night by enduring covenant

verses.text: The sun returns and enters the second eastern portal. It travels again through these divisions of its course for thirty mornings, rising and setting.
verses.study: The second portal is revisited on the return toward equal day. Rising and setting faithfully retrace the ordered path.
crossReferences: Psalm 113:3 — the Lord is praised from sunrise to sunset
Ecclesiastes 3:15 — what has been returns within God's ordering

verses.text: On that day the night is shortened in length. The night becomes ten parts, and the day eight parts.
verses.study: The balance shifts steadily toward greater light. Numbered time gives witness to consistent order.
crossReferences: Genesis 1:14 — lights measure days and seasons
Psalm 90:12 — numbered days can form wise hearts

verses.text: On that day the sun rises through that portal and sets in the west. It returns east and rises through the third portal for thirty-one mornings, and it sets in the west of heaven.
verses.study: The last listed portal station brings the course back toward equality. The cycle closes where its opening movement can begin again.
crossReferences: Psalm 19:6 — nothing is hidden from the sun's circuit
Ecclesiastes 1:5 — the sun returns to its place of rising

verses.text: On that day the night is shortened and becomes nine parts, and the day nine parts. The night is equal to the day, and the year is exactly 364 days.
verses.study: Equal day and night coincide with the stated completion of the 364-day year. The calendar summarizes the ordered portal journey.
crossReferences: Genesis 1:14 — years are measured by heavenly lights
1 Chronicles 23:31 — worship follows appointed times throughout the year

verses.text: The length and shortness of day and night are distinguished through the course of the sun.
verses.study: The chapter identifies solar movement as the observable means by which changing daylight is known.
crossReferences: Psalm 104:19 — the sun knows its time of setting
Job 38:19–20 — light and darkness have their paths and places

verses.text: Because of it, the course of the day grows longer from day to day, while the course of the night grows shorter from night to night.
verses.study: Daily change accumulates within the larger pattern. Small differences serve an intelligible whole.
crossReferences: Zechariah 14:7 — day and night remain known to the Lord
Psalm 139:12 — darkness and light are alike before God

verses.text: This is the command and course of the sun, and its return when it returns sixty times and rises. It is the great light called the sun forever and ever.
verses.study: The sun's repeated return is named a command. Its greatness consists in enduring service, not independent sovereignty.
crossReferences: Psalm 148:3–6 — sun and moon praise by keeping God's decree
Jeremiah 31:35–36 — the sun's ordinance endures before the Lord

verses.text: This one that rises is the great light, named according to its appearance, just as the Lord commanded.
verses.study: Both the sun's name and appearance remain subordinate to the Lord's command. Created splendor points beyond itself.
crossReferences: Genesis 1:16 — the greater light is made by God
Psalm 84:11 — the Lord Himself is the ultimate source of light and favor

verses.text: As it rises, so it sets. It does not diminish or rest, but runs day and night in its chariot. Its light shines seven times brighter than the moon's light, though the two are equal in size.
verses.study: The closing comparison retains the vision's own cosmological description. Its theological emphasis is the sun's tireless fulfillment of its assigned course.
crossReferences: Psalm 19:5–6 — the sun runs its course like a strong runner
Isaiah 30:26 — the sun's light is pictured as sevenfold
Habakkuk 3:11 — sun and moon stand within God's sovereign action

explanation.heading: Chapter teaching and context
paragraphs: Chapter 72 opens the Astronomical Book as Uriel's ordered account of the heavenly lights. The six eastern and six western portals provide the vision's framework for describing the solar year.
The changing ratios of day and night are traced through alternating periods of thirty and thirty-one mornings. Increase, equality, decrease and return all belong to one intelligible cycle.
The stated 364-day year reflects the calendar presented by this ancient Geʽez witness. The translation preserves its numerical and portal system without forcing it into a later model of astronomy.
Throughout the chapter, the sun is magnificent but never divine. Wind drives its chariot, appointed portals govern its route, and its tireless rising and setting fulfill the Lord's command.

crossReferences: Genesis 1:14–18 — lights appointed for signs, seasons, days and years
Psalm 19:1–6 — the sun declares glory by running its circuit
Psalm 104:19–23 — sun and moon order creaturely time
Psalm 148:3–6 — heavenly lights keep the Creator's decree
Jeremiah 31:35–36 — the ordinances of the lights endure
Isaiah 65:17 — the promise of new creation
